SOURCE EXTRACT — read from the full djvu texts of ten volumes, 2026-09-06 (p_432)
=================================================================================
THE SCHOOL: A MAGAZINE DEVOTED TO ELEMENTARY AND SECONDARY EDUCATION
Toronto: University of Toronto / Ontario College of Education

This is the continuation of `1912-13-the-school-magazine-fh-spinney.txt`, which read volume 1
and ended with the note that "LATER VOLUMES OF THE SCHOOL, which ran to 1935 and are on the
Internet Archive, are UNSEARCHED — and the run covers every year of his known Kanawana service."
They are now searched.

WHAT WAS ENUMERATED AND WHAT WAS READ
-------------------------------------
The series was enumerated on the Internet Archive scrape API against the identifier stem
`schoolmagazinede*`. Eleven items exist: schoolmagazinede01univuoft through 11univuoft, with
VOLUME 3 MISSING FROM THE ARCHIVE, plus schoolmagazinede10ontauoft (a separate scan, 1935).
None is lending-restricted. Ten complete djvu texts were downloaded and searched in full
(volume 1 previously, volumes 2 and 4 through 11 in this pass).

Volume years are taken from each volume's own title page, NOT from the Internet Archive
metadata, which gives only the series span "1912-35" for every item:

  vol 1  Sept 1912 – June 1913      vol 7   Sept 1918 – June 1919
  vol 2  Sept 1913 – June 1914      vol 8   Sept 1919 – June 1920
  vol 3  Sept 1914 – June 1915      vol 9   Sept 1920 – June 1921
         NOT ON THE ARCHIVE — UNREAD
  vol 4  Sept 1915 – June 1916      vol 10  Sept 1921 – June 1922
  vol 5  Sept 1916 – June 1917      vol 11  Sept 1922 – June 1923
  vol 6  Sept 1917 – June 1918

EVERY ONE OF THESE YEARS IS READ OFF THE VOLUME'S OWN TITLE PAGE, which prints the span in the
form "VOLUME IV. / September, 1915 to June, 1916." — none is inferred from the series. Volume 3's
span is the only one stated here without a title page behind it, since the volume could not be
obtained; it is the gap between the dated volumes on either side of it.
`schoolmagazinede10ontauoft` (1935) was NOT read.

"KANAWANA" OCCURS ZERO TIMES IN ANY OF THE TEN VOLUMES
------------------------------------------------------
A clean null across 1912–1923, the whole of the camp's early and interwar era up to volume 11.
The magazine is a professional journal for teachers, not a general-interest one, so this is not
surprising; it is recorded so nobody searches it again.


I. HIS FIRST NAME IS FREDERICK
==============================
Volume 1 gave him only as "F. H. Spinney", and the cache file for it, this project's KB and
`wiki/people/directors-index.md` all recorded that his first name was not in any source found.

It is in volumes 2, 4 and 5, fourteen times, set in full capitals in the by-line:

    Letter Writing
    FREDERICK  H.  SPINNEY
    Principal,  Alexandra  Public  School,  Montreal
                                              — vol 2 (1913-14), scan line 12532

    In  the  Classroom
    FREDERICK  H.  SPINNEY
    Principal,  Alexandra  Public  School,  Montreal
                                              — vol 5 (1916-17), scan line 1333

A NOTE ON WHY IT WAS MISSED THE FIRST TIME, because it will happen again. The scan's OCR
double-spaces between words. A grep for `FREDERICK H. SPINNEY` with single spaces returns ZERO
in all ten volumes; `FREDERICK  H.  SPINNEY` returns fourteen. The name was in the corpus the
whole time and the query was wrong. Search these texts with `[[:space:]]\+` or a
case-insensitive substring, never with literal single spaces.

The volume-5 index and the vol-2 Round Table also print the initials-only form, so both forms
run concurrently; the full form is not a later correction of the short one.


II. HIS ADDRESS, AND HIS SCHOOL'S
=================================
Volume 2's Round Table prints his correspondence address (scan line 28774):

    [Extract from a letter re International Correspondence Scheme received from F. H. Spinney,
    160 Sanguinet Street, Montreal, Que.]

Volume 4 gives the same number as the school's (see III below): "the Alexandra School, 160
Sanguinet Street". So 160 Sanguinet is ALEXANDRA SCHOOL ITSELF, not his home — he was taking
his correspondence at his desk. This is a school address and should not be recorded as a
residence.

Sanguinet Street runs through what was then Montreal's Jewish immigrant quarter east of the
Main; volume 4 says the school's children "are nearly all of Jewish origin". That is the
magazine's characterisation of the pupils, printed in 1915, and it is quoted rather than
paraphrased.


III. THE FIND THAT MATTERS: HE TAUGHT BASKETRY
===============================================
The identification of the magazine's F. H. Spinney with Kamp Kanawana's Educational Director
previously rested on name, city and calling — a real but circumstantial join, and it was
written that way. Volume 4 supplies a fourth term that is not circumstantial, because it is
specific and odd.

This project's fact f_0058 records, from the 1922 camp brochure, that Kanawana's Educational
Director F.H. Spinney was TEACHING BASKETRY.

Volume 4 (Sept 1915 – June 1916), quoting the Montreal Daily Star of December 18th [1915],
scan line 30605:

    Over $125 was realized yesterday afternoon for the Canadian Red Cross Society at the sale
    of baskets held at the Alexandra School, 160 Sanguinet Street. The baskets were made by
    the pupils and teachers in the "after school" class which meets twice a week, from 3.30 to
    5 p.m. The idea originated with F. H. Spinney, the head master, who wished to see how the
    children would get on at hand work. About a year ago the class was started and now some
    fifteen teachers and fifty pupils work together making all sorts of baskets from little
    flower pots to big waste-paper baskets. The classrooms were beautifully decorated yesterday
    with all sorts of Christmas decorations made chiefly by the children, who are nearly all of
    Jewish origin. Three little girls and five boys gave a demonstration of the work in one of
    the rooms, and tea was served in another in which Miss White, one of the kindergarten
    mistresses, presided. Cake was contributed by the cooking centres. — Montreal Daily Star,
    of Dec. 18th.

The same uncommon surname, the same two initials, the same city, the same profession — and now
the same unusual specific activity, basketry taught to children out of school hours, six years
before the camp brochure records him teaching it at Kanawana, and started on his own initiative.

This is still an identification rather than a document naming both roles in one line. No source
found says "F. H. Spinney of Alexandra School is the Kanawana Educational Director". But the
join has moved from "plausible by name and calling" to "four independent points of agreement,
one of them a distinctive practice he personally introduced." It should be described that way
and not as proven.

It also dates the basketry to Montreal and to about the autumn of 1914 — he brought it TO the
camp, he did not pick it up there.


IV. THE FULL RUN OF HIS CONTRIBUTIONS, AND WHERE IT STOPS
=========================================================
By-lines, with the heading each sits under, read from the scans:

VOLUME 1 (1912-13) — "In the Little Red Schoolhouse", at least eight numbered instalments
  on the practice of the one-room rural school. The editors announce a second series.
  (Read previously; see the volume-1 cache file.)

VOLUME 2 (1913-14) — 11 by-lines:
  "Little Journeys to Rural Schools" ×8 (lines 1730, 4849, 8208, 11623, 16060, 20216, 28341,
      31167). THE SECOND SERIES ANNOUNCED IN VOLUME 1 WAS IN FACT WRITTEN. The volume-1 cache
      file lists "whether the second series was ever written" as not established; it is now.
  "Letter Writing" ×1 (12532) — the first appearance of the full first name.
  "The Use of our Holidays" ×1 (34563).
  A signed Round Table letter (28788) soliciting pupils' letters nationally.

VOLUME 3 (1914-15) — NOT ON THE INTERNET ARCHIVE. UNREAD. This is a real hole, not a null.

VOLUME 4 (1915-16) — 10 by-lines:
  "In the Classroom" ×4 (2488, 6394, 12426, 36911)
  "Letter Writing" ×6 (2910, 16179, 16797, 26746, 31732, 45368) — his International
      Correspondence Scheme, exchanging pupils' letters "from all over Canada, from every State
      in the American Union, and from many parts of England".
  Plus the Montreal Daily Star basketry item quoted in III, which is ABOUT him rather than by him.

VOLUME 5 (1916-17) — 8 by-lines, all "In the Classroom", a lesson-by-lesson series largely on
  teaching Fractions to a Fifth Grade divided into three ability groups.

VOLUME 6 (1917-18)  — "Spinney" occurs ZERO times.
VOLUME 7 (1918-19)  — ZERO.
VOLUME 8 (1919-20)  — ZERO.
VOLUME 11 (1922-23) — ZERO.

VOLUMES 9 (1920-21) AND 10 (1921-22) CONTAIN "SPINNEY" AND IT IS NOT HIM. Both are Nova
Scotians and neither is a Montreal schoolmaster:
  vol 9, lines 1781 and 40152: "Hon. E. K. Spinney, member for Yarmouth and Clare, N.S.",
      listed as a Minister without Portfolio — Edgar Keith Spinney, in the Meighen ministry.
  vol 10, line 9873: the same man, in a later cabinet list.
  vol 10, line 8144: "Miss Catherine Spinney has transferred herself from Truro to Halifax."
These are recorded because a future search on the bare surname will hit them, and a careless
reading of volume 9 or 10 could put Kanawana's Educational Director in the federal cabinet.

SO: HIS CONTRIBUTIONS RUN FROM VOLUME 1 TO VOLUME 5 AND STOP DEAD IN JUNE 1917.
He published in the magazine continuously for five years and then never again in the six
volumes that follow, through June 1923.

The 1921 camp brochure documents him at Kanawana IN HIS FIFTH YEAR, which puts his first camp
season in 1917. His last piece for The School and his first summer at Kanawana fall in the same
year.

WHAT THAT IS AND IS NOT. It is a coincidence in date between two independently documented
series, and it is recorded as one. It is NOT evidence that the camp caused him to stop writing,
and the magazine gives no reason for his disappearance from it — no valedictory note, no
"Mr. Spinney has resigned", nothing. Volumes 6 through 11 also carry no successor at Alexandra
School, Montreal: every post-volume-5 "Alexandra School" in the run is a different school
elsewhere (Edmonton, Calgary, Moose Jaw, Lindsay), so the magazine simply stops covering the
Montreal one. The correct statement is that THE MAGAZINE STOPS MENTIONING HIM AFTER JUNE 1917,
not that he left the school.


V. WHAT IS STILL NOT ESTABLISHED
================================
- His surname initial H. still stands for nothing found.
- His birth and death dates, and any record of him outside this magazine and the camp brochures.
- Whether he stayed at Alexandra School after 1917. The magazine's silence is not his departure.
- When he left Kanawana, beyond the 1922 brochure being the last to name him.
- Volume 3 (1914-15) is not on the Internet Archive and has not been read anywhere.
- Volumes 12 onward (1923-1935) exist as a run but only the 1935 scan
  (`schoolmagazinede10ontauoft`) was found on the Archive; it was not read. By 1923 he has been
  absent from the magazine for six years, so the expected yield is low, but it is not zero and
  it has not been checked.

QUERIES RUN AGAINST THE TEN TEXTS: case-insensitive `kanawana` (0 in all ten); `spinney`
(counts by volume: 17, 12, —, 11, 8, 0, 0, 0, 3, 2, 0); `frederick` within three lines of
`spinney`; `alexandra +school`; `little +journeys`; `in +the +classroom`; `letter +writing`;
and title-page scans for the volume years.

`basket` was run against the four volumes that carry Spinney at all (10, 5, 20 and 26 hits in
volumes 1, 2, 4 and 5) and cross-filtered for Alexandra, Sanguinet, Spinney and Montreal. THE
DECEMBER 1915 STAR ITEM IS THE ONLY BASKETRY PASSAGE CONNECTED TO HIM in the run; the other
hits are wastepaper baskets, basket-work in other provinces' schools, and the like. So the
basketry join rests on one printed paragraph, not on a pattern of them, and III should be read
with that in mind.
